english.title: Have article with intent to destroy / damage property - endanger life

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: possess article to commit criminal damage. possess article to commit criminal damage

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) had in your custody or under your control **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE..) intending without lawful excuse to use the same or to cause or permit another to use the same to

(A)_[destroy]_
(B)_[damage]_

property, namely **(..SPECIFY PROPERTY..) belonging to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) in a way which you knew was likely to endanger the life of **(..SPECIFY NAME OF VICTIM..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 3(b) and 4 of the Criminal Damage Act 1971.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)

english.notes:
(i) Property to be damaged/destroyed must be that of the defendant's or user(s) of article(s).
(ii) '**(..SPECIFY PERSON..)' will, therefore, invariably be 'you', though on occasion will be the name of the user/intended user of the article(s).

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Ten years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
